chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to him, 'Inform me about the extent of the face which is befitting for one to wash for the Ablution (Wudu) which Allah (Exalted and Majestic) speaks of?' So he said: 'The face which Allah (the Exalted) commanded with its washing is that which is not befitting for anyone to increase upon, nor be deficient from it; if he exceeds upon it, he would not be recompensed, and if he is deficient from it, he would sin. [It is] what the index finger, the middle finger, and the thumb would circumvent from the front of the head to the chin, and what the two fingers flow upon from the face, encircling, so it is from the face, and whatever is besides that, so it is not from the face.' I said, 'The temples (sides of the forehead) is not from the face?' He said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: What is the exact definition of the face area to be washed in Wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the definitive anatomical boundaries for the face in Wudu, specifying the area from the hairline to the chin and including the temples, as determined by the span of the index, middle, and thumb fingers. It emphasizes the principle of 'no increase or decrease' (la ziyada wa la nuqsan), a key juristic concept ensuring that the ritual act is neither incomplete nor excessive, thereby securing the validity and reward of the ablution.
